# INTRODUCTION.

->§ I.<-

How brilliantly and usefully the secular disciplines—all those that constitute a general education <note>original Greek: ἐγκύκλιον παιδείαν (*enkyklion paideian*). This refers to the "circle of arts and sciences" that formed the basis of a classical liberal education.</note>—can be applied to adorn the temple of God like the spoils of Egypt <note>A popular theological metaphor based on Exodus 12:35–36; it suggests that just as the Israelites took Egyptian gold to build the Tabernacle, Christians may use "pagan" or secular knowledge to support the Gospel.</note> is made manifest by the scholarly works of those who, especially in our own time, have devoted all their study and effort to transferring outside learning <note>original Greek: τὰ ἔξωθεν μαθήματα (*ta exōthen mathēmata*), referring to non-religious or secular studies.</note> to sacred use. Indeed, this is confirmed by the very clear testimonies of the most famous lights of the early Church: Basil, Jerome, Photius, Eustathius, and others. Furthermore, it is not only Greek and Roman letters, but also Eastern literature, which [brings] incredible [benefit] to the sacred scriptures <note>original: "sanctiores pandectas." Wolle uses the legal term *Pandects* (a compendium of Roman law) as a metaphor for the Bible as the definitive collection of divine law.</note> so that they might be more readily...

Thus, undying thanks are owed both to those interpreters of the **NEW COVENANT** <note>original Latin: "Novi Foederis," a standard term for the New Testament.</note> who are skilled in secular antiquity, and especially to certain more recent philologists. These scholars, equipped with the necessary knowledge of Eastern literature and especially of Jewish ceremonies, have brought both equal learning and industry to the task of explaining the sacred records <note>original Greek: "ὑπομνήματα" (*hypomnēmata*), meaning memoirs or accounts, here referring to the Gospels and Epistles.</note> of the New Covenant. 

Since the **ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE** <note>original Greek: "CΥΝΑΓΩΓΗC" (*Synagōgēs*).</note> of the Jews—that is, the house sacred to divine worship where they gathered, especially on the Sabbaths, to hear the reading and interpretation of the Law and the Prophets and to perform other sacred duties—is mentioned so frequently in the New Covenant, anyone who intends to properly fulfill the role of an interpreter of the divine oracles considers it entirely his duty to have an accurate and thorough understanding of synagogal ceremonies. 

This particular glory has been earned above all others by **CAMPEGIUS VITRINGA** <note>A prominent Dutch theologian (1659–1722) whose work on the synagogue remains a primary source for understanding early Jewish and Christian worship.</note>, the most celebrated doctor of the so-called Reformed Church. He has served the Christian commonwealth excellently and remarkably, not only through his other highly learned writings but especially through this very work: a most elaborate monument *On the Ancient Synagogue*, which has given us the occasion to bring it to light once again. 

Before I begin to review the occasion for writing this book and the specifics of the present edition, I trust my efforts will not be useless if I explain the **USE** and **ABUSE** of the **ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE** in the **INTERPRETATION OF THE NEW COVENANT** in a brief account. I promise and undertake to do this to the best of my ability, with the hand of God <note>original Greek: "Θεῷ σὺν παλάμᾳ" (*Theō syn palama*), a poetic way of saying "with God's help."</note>.

->§. II.<-

But I perceive quite clearly that this question of no small importance—*whether there is any Use and Abuse of the Ancient Synagogue in the most holy Pandects <note>A "Pandect" usually refers to a complete body of laws; here, Wolle uses it to describe the New Testament as the complete record of divine law.</note> of the New Covenant?*—must be weighed by me before I approach the treatment of the subject itself. For one might not unreasonably hesitate, and might judge that he who could demonstrate that all the Greek words <note>original Greek: "λέξεις" (*lexeis*).</note> of the New Covenant can be rendered clear and explained solely from the ancient writers of Greece would be performing a far more useful task and one more glorious for the character and nature of the sacred style. 

However, just as I am persuaded and have clearly discovered that certain varieties and elegances of the Greek dialects—namely Attic, Ionic, Doric, and Aeolic (which has the closest affinity with Boeotian)—are found in these most holy documents; so too, an inspection of the texts forbids anyone to doubt that the divinely inspired <note>original Greek: "θεόπνευστα" (*theopneusta*).</note> writings of the New Instrument <note>Another term for the New Testament.</note> display certain Jewish phrases that savor of a Hebrew-Chaldean idiom <note>original Greek: "ἰδίωμα" (*idiōma*).</note>. I believe that both of these things occurred by the most wise counsel of the **IMMORTAL DEITY**. For the Greek phraseology, distinguished by various dialects, in

Furthermore, the **MOST EXCELLENT AND MIGHTY SAVIOR**, as He himself frequently entered the Jewish **SYNAGOGUE** <note>original Greek: "ΣΥΝΑΓΩΓΗΣ" (*synagōgēs*)</note>, possessed an excellent and deep understanding of its praiseworthy customs as well as its abuses, and He rightly considered it part of His role to sternly rebuke the latter. The **EVANGELISTS** have recorded the history of these events in the woven monuments of their writings. Nor do we fail to understand from the commentaries of **LUKE**, which contain the **Acts of the Holy Apostles** <note>original Greek: "πράξεις τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων" (*praxeis tōn hagiōn Apostolōn*)</note>, that the **APOSTLES**—**PETER**, **PAUL**, **BARNABAS**, and others—frequently entered Jewish synagogues to explain the Gospel of **JESUS CHRIST** to the assembly present there. In such fields, therefore, I believe no one will attempt to deny that the **ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE** commends itself through its remarkable usefulness.

Since men of great reputation—**HUGO GROTIUS**, **JOHN LIGHTFOOT**, **JOHN SPENCER**, **STEPHANUS LE MOINE**, and our own **VITRINGA**, as well as many others whose names the most celebrated theologian of Tübingen today, **CHRISTOPH MATTHÄUS PFAFF**, (*) recounts with great learning—seem to believe they have significant reasons for deriving the origins of all **CHRISTIAN** as well as Apostolic discipline from the synagogue, I am now going to discuss how this comparison should be established cautiously and "with a grain of salt" <note>A Latin idiom (*cum grano salis*) meaning to treat something with skepticism or careful judgment.</note>. It is easy to wander from the path of truth here, as few monuments remain that show the true face of the ancient synagogue. For everything relevant to this matter must be drawn both from the **Talmudic** <term>Talmud: The central text of Rabbinic Judaism, containing records of legal discussions and traditions.</term> collections—which are not particularly long on this subject—and from the most holy Scripture of the **NEW COVENANT** itself. 

Since these sources are beyond all controversy, I see that one thing remains: to explain in two sections the genuine **USE** of the **ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE IN THE INTERPRETATION OF THE NEW COVENANT**, and its **ABUSE** which must be avoided. The first section will address the **USE** and **ABUSE** in the **phrasing** <note>original Greek: "φράσει" (*phrasei*), referring here to the style of language, idioms, and expression.</note> of the New Covenant; the second will examine the comparison between the discipline of **CHRIST** and the **APOSTOLIC** discipline presented in the New Covenant and that of the **ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE**. In both parts, I have decided to adopt this rule of discourse: to encompass the entire matter within certain rules—which I will explain more fully where they lack clarity—and to illustrate them with selected examples. Therefore, [the first section] will deal with...

<meta>This page continues Christopher Wolle's preliminary dissertation on the Jewish Synagogue's influence on the New Testament. The previous page established that Jesus and the Apostles were familiar with synagogue customs; this page begins the formal "First Section," introducing the first rule for linguistic interpretation: using the synagogue's cultural context to define specific New Testament terms for converts and "God-fearers."</meta>

<header>PRELIMINARY DISSERTATION ON THE USE AND ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE</header>

# FIRST SECTION
## ON THE USE AND ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE IN EXPLAINING THE PHRASING OF THE NEW TESTAMENT. <note>The author uses "N. F." as an abbreviation for *Novum Foedus*, the New Covenant or New Testament.</note>

### RULE I.

The Ancient Synagogue is of use if those words <note>original Greek: "λέξεις" (*lexeis*)</note> and phrases of the New Testament are accurately <note>original Greek: "ἀκριβῶς" (*akribōs*)</note> illustrated from the synagogue—specifically those which the context <note>original Greek: "συνάφεια" (*synapheia*)</note> of the sacred text itself clearly shows to have been drawn from the usage of the ancient synagogue.

For no interpretation, which does not derive support from the context itself and its preceding and following passages, should be accepted as true and proven—even if it appears brilliant and is subtly crafted. Thus, a contrast <note>original Greek: "ἀντίθεσις" (*antithesis*)</note> is frequent and repeated several times in the records of the New Testament, where, for example:

ACTS 2:5; 8:2; 10:22; 13:16, 26, 43; 16:14; 17:4, 17; 18:7. Sometimes **DEVOUT MEN** <note>original Greek: "ΕΥΛΑΒΕΙΣ" (*eulabeis*)</note> "from every nation," sometimes **THOSE WHO FEAR GOD** <note>original Greek: "ΦΟΒΟΥΜΕΝΟΙ ΤΟΝ ΘΕΟΝ" (*phoboumenoi ton theon*)</note>, sometimes **WORSHIPPERS** <note>original Greek: "ΣΕΒΟΜΕΝΟΙ" (*sebomenoi*)</note>, and *Jews* in the synagogue are set in opposition to one another. This very contrast provides a most clear opportunity to suspect that such a designation was once not unusual in the Jewish synagogue. And indeed, it is remarkably so: for in the Talmudic records there are mentioned very frequently not only the <term>Pious of the nations of the world</term> <note>original Hebrew: "חסידי אומות עולם" (*Chassidei Umot HaOlam*)</note>, but also <term>those who fear the LORD</term> <note>original Hebrew: "יראי יהוה" (*Yirei Hashem*)</note>, as attested by the master of the Hebrew nation, **MAIMONIDES** in the Talmudic treatise *Melakim* <note>The "Laws of Kings"</note>, chapter 10. See also **PIERRE JURIEU** in his *Critical History of Doctrines and Cults, Good and Bad, part I, chapters 6 and 7.* By that name, those from among the pagans were primarily designated by the *Jews* who were <term>Proselytes of the gate</term> <note>original Hebrew: "גרי תושב" (*Gerei Toshav*); these were Gentiles who followed the Seven Laws of Noah but did not undergo full conversion or circumcision</note>; that is, those who, without having accepted circumcision and other Jewish ceremonies, but having abjured **idolatry** <note>original Greek: "εἰδωλολατρείᾳ" (*eidololatreia*)</note> and having been commanded to cast far away the **worship of many gods** <note>original Greek: "πολυθεότητι" (*polytheotēti*)</note>, piously worshipped the one GOD. For this reason, just as they occupied the "Court of the Gentiles" in the Temple, they also occupied a specific place in the synagogue. These same people—for the reason that they were not entirely Jews—are called

ROMANS 1:16; 2:9, 10; 3:9; 10:12; and additionally ACTS 14:1, **GREEKS** <note>original Greek: "ΕΛΛΗΝΕΣ" (*Hellenes*)</note>, as the same contrast proves. Therefore, they are not to be confused with *the Jews* or with *the Gentiles* <note>meaning the completely unconverted pagans</note>, as **SALMASIUS** and others have noted.

<meta>Catchword: RULE-</meta>

<summary>This page defines the first rule for interpreting New Testament language, arguing that terms for Gentile converts like "God-fearers" or "Greeks" are best understood through the specific social categories used in the ancient Jewish synagogue. It identifies these groups as "Proselytes of the Gate" who worshipped the one God without adopting the full Mosaic Law.</summary>
<keywords>Proselytes of the Gate, God-fearers, Maimonides, Rule of Interpretation, Philology, Acts of the Apostles, Greeks vs Jews, Synagogue usage</keywords>

<meta>This page continues Christopher Wolle’s "Preliminary Dissertation," following the introduction of Rule I. Whereas the first rule discussed the proper use of the Ancient Synagogue in interpreting the New Testament, this page introduces Rule II, which warns against the "abuse" or over-application of Jewish customs to the Greek text where the context does not warrant it.</meta>

<header>ON THE INTERPRETATION OF THE NEW COVENANT.</header>

# RULE II.

## It is an **ABUSE** of Sacred Scripture if invented emphases <note>original Greek: "ἐμφάσεις" (*emphaseis*)</note> and foreign notions sought from the synagogue are attributed to the words <note>original Greek: "λέξεσιν" (*lexesin*)</note> and phrases <note>original Greek: "φράσεσι" (*phrasesi*)</note> of the New Testament, where the sacred context says absolutely nothing <note>original Greek: "οὐδὲ γρῦ" (*oude gry*) — literally "not even a grunt," an idiom for "not a single word."</note> about the synagogue.

For by this reasoning, the sense is not so much drawn out as it is forced in; indeed, the empty conjectures of human wit are sold as the sense of the HOLY SPIRIT: something which is alien to the duty of a genuine interpreter of sacred literature. I will mention a few words as they come to hand. There are learned men who <margin>LUKE 1:35.</margin> contend that the force and emphasis of the word **TO OVERSHADOW** <note>original Greek: "ΕΠΙΣΚΙΑΖΕΙΝ" (*episkiazein*)</note> must be unfolded from the rite of the **CHUPPAH** <note>A canopy used in Jewish wedding ceremonies to symbolize the home the couple will share.</note>, once used in the synagogal betrothal, through a metaphor that is—in my judgment—harsh and far-fetched.

But read and re-read the sacred history; the Jewish *chuppah* will never come to your mind. Yet I suffer all these men to be satisfied with their own sense; provided they also grant me the indulgence of more easily clarifying the power <note>original Greek: "δεινότητα" (*deinotēta*)</note> hidden in that word. Turning therefore to the very scrolls of the New Testament, three times—namely in *Matthew* 17:5, *Mark* 9:7, and *Luke* 9:34—I find the verb "to overshadow" used regarding a bright cloud. For it is said, as MARK has it, "a cloud **OVERSHADOWING** them" <note>original Greek: "νεφέλη ΕΠΙΣΚΙΑΖΟΥΣΑ αὐτοῖς" (*nephelē episkiazousa autois*)</note>; a bright cloud provided a covering for *them*, namely the Apostles, on the mountain of the transfiguration of CHRIST: by the benefit of which covering <note>original Greek: "σκεπάσματος" (*skepasmatos*)</note> or shade they were able to bear the rays of the divine majesty present in the cloud. 

In exactly the same way, and with the same construction, the messenger of the heavenly birth of JESUS CHRIST says to MARY the Mother of God <note>original Greek: "Θεοτόκῳ" (*Theotokō*) — literally "God-bearer."</note>: "**The power of the Highest SHALL OVERSHADOW you**" <note>original Greek: "Δύναμις ὑψίστου ΕΠΙΣΚΙΑΣΕΙ σοι" (*Dynamis hypsistou episkiasei soi*)</note>, that is, *the power of the Most High will provide a covering for you*, so that you may best be able to bear the most shining rays of the majesty of THE SON OF GOD to be born from your womb. And by this reasoning, the "coming upon" <note>original Greek: "ἐπέλευσις" (*epeleusis*)</note> of the HOLY SPIRIT mentioned shortly before is expressed by this much more significant word "overshadowing" <note>original Greek: "ἐπισκιάσεως" (*episkiaseōs*)</note> according to the thorough working out <note>original Greek: "κατ᾽ ἐξεργασίαν" (*kat’ exergasian*) — a rhetorical term for elaborating on a theme.</note> most common to the sacred writers. For in this way, "the Power of the Highest" must be explained as the HOLY SPIRIT, who is also vigorously called "Power from on high" <note>original Greek: "Δύναμις ἐξ ὕψους" (*Dynamis ex hypsous*)</note> in *Luke* 24:49. This interpretation, which corresponds both to the force of the word and to parallel passages, also [leads to the] angelic...

(*) Thus "coming upon" <note>original Greek: "ἐπιφοίτησις" (*epiphoitēsis*)</note>, which word in the glosses of PHILOXENUS signifies *appearance*, and is used by CHRYSOSTOM concerning *the advent of the HOLY SPIRIT under the image of a dove* (Sermon 74, volume 5, page 526), is—according to the interpreter HESYCHIUS—a "COMING UPON" <note>original Greek: "ΕΠΕΛΕΥΣΙΣ" (*epeleusis*)</note> or "presence" <note>original Greek: "παρουσία" (*parousia*)</note>. Furthermore, this very "coming upon" and "overshadowing" altogether surpasses all understanding <note>original Greek: "πᾶσαν κατάληψιν" (*pasan katalēpsin*)</note>.

<header>PRELIMINARY DISSERTATION ON THE USE AND ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE</header>

# SECTION ONE
## ON THE USE AND ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE IN EXPLAINING THE PHRASEOLOGY OF THE NEW TESTAMENT.
### RULE I.

->*The Ancient Synagogue has USE [is helpful] if those words <note>original Greek: "λέξεις" (*lexeis*)</note> and phrases <note>original Greek: "φράσεις" (*phraseis*)</note> of the New Testament <note>abbreviated as N. F. for *Novum Foedus*</note> are precisely <note>original Greek: "ἀκριβῶς" (*akribōs*)</note> illustrated, which the context <note>original Greek: "συνάφεια" (*synapheia*)</note> of the sacred text itself clearly shows to have been derived from the use of the ancient synagogue.*<-

For no interpretation, which does not take its defense from the context itself, and from its preceding and following parts, should be admitted as true and proven, even if it appears brilliant and is subtly devised. Thus, there is a frequent and repeatedly used antithesis <note>original Greek: "ἀντίθεσις" — a contrast or opposition</note> in the books <note>literally "pandects," a term for a complete body of laws or writings</note> of the New Testament, by which, for example,

ACTS 2:5; 8:2; 10:22; 13:16, 26, 43; 16:14; 17:4, 17; 18:7, sometimes **DEVOUT MEN FROM EVERY NATION** <note>original Greek: "ΕΥΛΑΒΕΙΣ ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους" (*Eulabeis apo pantos ethnous*)</note>, sometimes **THOSE FEARING GOD** <note>original Greek: "ΦΟΒΟΥΜΕΝΟΙ ΤΟΝ ΘΕΟΝ" (*Phoboumenoi ton Theon*)</note>, sometimes **WORSHIPPERS** <note>original Greek: "ΣΕΒΟΜΕΝΟΙ" (*Sebomenoi*)</note>, and **Jews** in the synagogue are contrasted with one another. This very antithesis provides a most clear opportunity to suspect that such a naming convention was once common in the Jewish synagogue. This is exceptionally so: for in the Talmudic books, not only are the **pious of the nations of the world** <note>original Hebrew: "חסידי אומות עולם" (*chasidei umot ha'olam*)</note> mentioned very often, but also the **fearers of the LORD** <note>original Hebrew: "יראי יהוה" (*yirai Yehovah*)</note>, as testified by the teacher of the Hebrew nation, MAIMONIDES <note>A preeminent medieval Sephardic Jewish philosopher and scholar</note> in the Talmudic treatise *Melakim* [Kings], chapter 90. Add Pierre Jurieu, *Critical History of Dogmas and Worships, Good and Bad, part I, chapters VI and VII.* By that name, the Jews primarily designated those among the pagans who were **sojourning proselytes** <note>original Hebrew: "גרי תושב" (*gere toshav*)</note>, that is, **proselytes of the gate**. These were people who, while not accepting circumcision and other Jewish ceremonies, had renounced idolatry <note>original Greek: "εἰδωλολατρείᾳ" (*eidololatreia*)</note> and had been commanded to cast away polytheism <note>original Greek: "πολυθεότητι" (*polytheotēti*)</note>, worshipping the one GOD devoutly. For this reason, just as there was a "court of the Gentiles" in the Temple, they occupied a special place in the synagogue. For the same reason, because they were not entirely Jews, they are called in

ROMANS 1:16; 2:9, 10; 3:9; 10:12; and also ACTS 14:1, **GREEKS** <note>original Greek: "ἝΛΛΗΝΕΣ" (*Hellēnes*)</note>, as the same antithesis proves. They are therefore not to be confused with the Jews, nor with the Gentiles <note>original Greek: "ἔθνεσι" (*ethnesi*) — the broader pagan world</note>, as [Claude] Saumaise <note>Salmasius</note> and others have noted.

<summary>This page introduces the first rule of New Testament interpretation regarding the use of Jewish synagogal context, arguing that such references are only valid when supported by the biblical text itself. It specifically applies this to the category of "God-fearers" or "Proselytes of the Gate"—Gentiles who worshipped God without fully converting to Judaism.</summary>

<meta>The previous page established Rule I, which argued that Jewish synagogue customs *should* be used to interpret the New Testament when the text explicitly references them. This page introduces Rule II, which warns against the opposite error: forcing Jewish customs into the text where they do not naturally belong.</meta>

ON THE INTERPRETATION OF THE NEW TESTAMENT.

## RULE II.

It is an ABUSE of the Ancient Synagogue if artificial emphases <note>original Greek: "ἐμφάσεις" (*emphases*)</note> and foreign notions fetched from the synagogue are attributed to the words <note>original Greek: "λέξεσιν" (*lexesin*)</note> and phrases <note>original Greek: "φράσεσι" (*phrasesi*) </note> of the New Testament <note>abbreviated as N. F. for *Novum Foedus*</note>, where nevertheless not a single word <note>original Greek: "οὐδὲ γρῦ" (*oude gry*) — literally "not even a grunt"</note> about the synagogue is read in the sacred context.

For by this reasoning, the sense is not so much brought out as it is brought in; indeed, the empty conjectures of human wit are sold as the meaning of the HOLY SPIRIT. Such a practice is foreign to the duty of a genuine interpreter of the sacred letters. I will describe a few words as they come to hand. For instance, there are learned men who contend that the force and emphasis of the word **OVERSHADOW** <note>original Greek: "ΕΠΙΣΚΙΑΖΕΙΝ" (*episkiazein*)</note> in LUKE 1:35 must be unfolded from the rite of the **CHUPPAH** <note>a Jewish wedding canopy</note>, which was once customary in synagogal betrothals. In my judgment, this is a harsh and far-fetched metaphor. Read and reread the sacred history, and the Jewish *chuppah* will never come to your mind. Yet, I allow all these men to be fully convinced in their own mind with a calm spirit, provided they also grant me the permission to more easily explain the hidden power <note>original Greek: "δεινότητα" (*deinotēta*)</note> in that word.

Therefore, turning through the very books <note>literally "pandects," a term for a complete body of writings</note> of the New Testament, I find the verb *overshadow* <note>original Greek: "ἐπισκιάζειν" (*episkiazein*)</note> used three times regarding a bright cloud, namely in *Matthew 17:5, Mark 9:7, and Luke 9:34.* For it is said, as MARK has it, **A CLOUD OVERSHADOWING THEM** <note>original Greek: "νεφέλη ΕΠΙΣΚΙΑΖΟΥΣΑ αὐτοῖς" (*nephelē episkiazousa autois*)</note>; that is, a bright cloud provided a shelter for *them* (namely the Apostles) on the mountain of the transfiguration of CHRIST. By the benefit of this covering <note>original Greek: "σϰέπασματος" (*skepasmatos*)</note> or shelter, they were able to endure the rays of the divine majesty present in the cloud.

In clearly the same way and with the same construction, the messenger of the heavenly birth of JESUS CHRIST says to MARY, the **Mother of God** <note>original Greek: "Θεοτόϰῳ" (*Theotokō*)</note>: **The power of the Most High SHALL OVERSHADOW you** <note>original Greek: "Δύναμις ὑψίστου ΕΠΙΣΚΙΑΣΕΙ σοι" (*Dynamis hypsistou episkiasei soi*)</note>. This means: *the power of the Altissimi will provide a shelter for you*, so that you may best be able to endure the most shining rays of the majesty of the SON OF GOD who is to be born from your womb. And by this reasoning, the "coming upon" <note>original Greek: "ἐπέλευσις" (*epeleusis*)</note> of the HOLY SPIRIT mentioned just before is expressed by this much more significant word "overshadowing," through a detailed elaboration <note>original Greek: "ϰατ᾽ ἐξεργασίαν" (*kat' exergasian*)</note> very common to the sacred writers. For in this way, "Power of the Most High" must be explained as the HOLY SPIRIT, who is also forcefully called "Power from on high" <note>original Greek: "Δύναμις ἐξ ὕψους" (*Dynamis ex hypsous*) in Luke 24:49</note>. This interpretation, which corresponds both to the force of the word and to parallel passages, also [leads to] the angelic...

---

(*) Thus "visitation" <note>original Greek: "ἐπιφοίτησις" (*epiphoitēsis*)</note>, a word which in the glosses of PHILOXENUS signifies an *apparition*, and is used by CHRYSOSTOM concerning the *arrival of the HOLY SPIRIT under the image of a dove* (Oration 74, volume 5, page 526), is, according to the interpreter HESYCHIUS, a **COMING UPON** <note>original Greek: "ΕΠΕΛΕΥΣΙΣ" (*epeleusis*)</note> or a presence <note>original Greek: "παρουσία" (*parousia*)</note>. Moreover, this very "coming upon" as well as the "overshadowing" altogether surpasses **all understanding** <note>original Greek: "πᾶσαν κατάληψιν" (*pasan katalēpsin*)</note>.
(†) Compare, if you please, my dissertation *on the use and abuse of the hermeneutic rules concerning equivalence or synonymy.*

->PRELIMINARY DISSERTATION ON THE USE AND ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE.<-

...it even connects the thread of the discourse most beautifully with the following particle "Therefore" <note>original Greek: "ΔΙΟ" (*dio*)</note> and so forth: however, I intentionally leave the more refined consideration and contemplation of this matter to the pious and learned reader.

**I CORINTHIANS 11:10.** SAINT PAUL writes as follows: "For this reason, a woman **ought to have authority on her head because of the ANGELS** <note>original Greek: "ΑΓΓΕΛΟΥΣ" (*angelous*)</note>." Here, a Dutch theologian of no small reputation, JOHANNES BRAUN, translates the phrase "to have authority on her head" into Latin as "to have power over her head." He explains this "power" of the woman as the freedom to uncover her head and her entire face. He further argues that by "the angels," the "messengers of the betrothal" <note>original Hebrew: "שלוחי קדושים" (*shelochi kedoshim*)</note> are indicated, as the TALMUDIC writers speak of them, especially in the volume *Kiddushin* <note>a section of the Talmud dealing with betrothal and marriage</note>. Braun stretches every nerve of his intellect to prove this in his *Selected Sacred Works*, Book I, Chapter III, page 62 and following. His argument is that the economy of the Old Covenant <note>abbreviated as V. F. for *Vetus Foedus*</note> was such that Jews stood before GOD "wrapped up" <note>original Hebrew: "מתעטפים" (*metatepim*)</note>, and prayed with their heads covered out of "reverence due to the Divine Presence" <note>original Hebrew: "מאימת שכינה" (*m'eimat shechinah*)</note>; likewise, it was a solemn custom that they had their own prayer shawl <note>original Hebrew: "טלית" (*tallit*) — a fringed garment worn during prayer</note> in the synagogue, with which they were veiled. See the Talmudic volumes *Shabbat*, folio 12, 1, and *Taanit*, folio 14, 2. To this may be added the learned commentaries <note>original Greek: "σχόλια" (*scholia*)</note> of MAIMONIDES <note>a preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher and scholar</note>. However, Braun claims that in the time of the New Covenant <note>abbreviated as N. F. for *Novum Foedus*</note>, women were granted the liberty of uncovering their heads IN THE PRESENCE OF the aforementioned "messengers" and the groom, for the sake of their beauty being seen.

But there are reasons ready at hand which stand against this interpretation <note>original Greek: "ἐξηγήσει" (*exēgēsei*)</note>. 

First, the divinely inspired writer <note>Paul</note> mentions absolutely nothing about synagogue ceremonies, but rather appeals to "what is proper" <note>original Greek: "τὸ πρέπον" (*to prepon*)</note> and "Christian decency" <note>original Greek: "εὐσχημοσύνην" (*euschēmosynēn*)</note>, and from there he seeks his arguments in verses 5, 6, and 13. Hence, we interpret the phrase "the woman ought," as cited in the verse, as "it is fitting for the woman." Thus PLATO explains "that which is owed" <note>original Greek: "τὸ ΟΦΕΙΛΟΜΕΝΟΝ" (*to opheilomenon*)</note> as "that which is fitting" <note>original Greek: "τὸ ΠΡΟΣΗΚΟΝ" (*to prosēkon*)</note> for one, in Book I of his *Politics*. GALEN, in his first commentary on Hippocrates' book *On the Nature of Man*, notes that "ought" <note>original Greek: "ΟΦΕΙΛΕΙ" (*opheilei*)</note>—for which he noticed "is accustomed" <note>original Greek: "φιλεῖ" (*philei*)</note> was read in other manuscripts—is explained as "it is fitting" <note>original Greek: "ΠΡΟΣΗΚΕΙ" (*prosēkei*)</note>. 

Furthermore, second, in Paul’s phrase, the word "on" <note>original Greek: "ΕΠΙ" (*epi*)</note> does not depend so much on "authority" as it does on the verb "to have": since "to have ON the head" <note>original Greek: "ἔχειν ΕΠΙ" (*echein epi*)</note>, just like in verse 4, "to have DOWN from the head" <note>original Greek: "ἔχειν ΚΑΤΑ" (*echein kata*)</note>, is the same as "to carry or wear upon the head," according to the interpretation of PHOTIUS, Patriarch of Constantinople. Add to this the summary by THEODORET included in CLEMENT OF ALEXANDRIA'S *Stromata*, Book VIII. This phrase, as it is properly used for a covering among Greek authors of better repute, is used here by PAUL in the same very elegant way. 

Third, as for the word "AUTHORITY" <note>original Greek: "ΕΞΟΥΣΙΑΝ" (*exousian*)</note>, which is "difficult to understand" <note>original Greek: "δυσνόητον" (*dysnoēton*)</note> and has been harassed by many interpreters of this oracle, we—setting aside the opinions of others—(*) explain the same in this place as "honor, dignity, glory,"

But in truth...

And I think that no compelling reason existed why he should have made up his mind to depart from the proper meaning of the noun **ANGELS** <note>original Greek: ΑΓΓΕΛΩΝ (*angelōn*)</note>, which in the New Testament is used absolutely—as here and in *Matthew 4:6, 11; 13:30; Acts 6:15; Hebrews 1:14* and elsewhere—to designate celestial spirits, to whom shame and reverence are owed everywhere, and especially in sacred assemblies. **Which was to be demonstrated.** <note>original Greek: Ὅ ἔδει δεῖξαι (*Ho edei deixai*); the Greek equivalent of the Latin Q.E.D.</note> For the rest, **JOHANNES**

ON THE INTERPRETATION OF THE NEW TESTAMENT.

D’ OUTREIN <note>Johannes d'Outrein (1662–1722), a Dutch theologian</note>, a most celebrated man, in his *theological-philological dissertation on the veiling of the woman's head because of the Angels at this passage,* which appears in the *Bremen Library, Class II, Booklet I, page 49 and following.*

## RULE III.

The **USE** of Sacred Scripture occurs if the **emphases** <note>original Greek: ἐμφάσεις (*emphaseis*)</note> of the **words** <note>original Greek: λέξεων (*lexeōn*)</note> and **phrases** <note>original Greek: φράσεων (*phraseōn*)</note> of the New Testament are carefully illustrated from certain and indubitable ceremonies of the synagogue which do not lack historical credibility; therefore, those writers who have described the rites of the Jewish synagogue are to be identified diligently and with all zeal.

For since the divinely revealed letters are **trustworthy** <note>original Greek: ἀξιόπισται (*axiopistai*)</note>, and are thus to be read thoroughly with the intent that they be accepted with indubitable faith, the matter speaks for itself: all sacred interpretations ought to aim toward establishing that kind of **demonstration** <note>original Greek: ἀπόδειξιν (*apodeixin*)</note>. Therefore, even synagogue antiquities, if any are to be applied to illustrate the books of the New Testament, must be free from doubt. I am about to relate an illustrative example.
In LUKE 2:46, JESUS CHRIST is recorded as **SITTING in the TEMPLE** <note>original Greek: ἐν τῷ ΙΕΡΩ ΚΑΘΕΖΟΜΕΝΟΣ (*en tō hierō kathezomenos*)</note>. In this place, beware of persuading yourself that he **SAT IN THE SANCTUARY ITSELF** <note>original Hebrew: היכל (*Heichal*, the inner Temple building)</note>; for this was granted to no one, except for kings descended from the family of David, to whom the power of **SITTING** was given. Rather, it is understood as the **HOUSE OF ASSEMBLY** <note>original Hebrew: בית הכנסת (*Beit HaKnesset*)</note>, or the **SYNAGOGUE OF THE TEMPLE**, which was near the courtyard, according to Rabbi Solomon Iarchi <note>The famous commentator Rashi</note> in his notes on the tractate *Yoma, chapter VII, section I.* As a witness of that custom of **SITTING**, I have an authority of great weight, MAIMONIDES <note>The preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher and jurist</note>, a man most skilled in ancient Jewish rites, in his *commentaries on the Mishnaic tractate Yoma, chapter VII, section I*; and likewise Rabbi OBADIAH DE BARTENORA <note>Bertinoro, a 15th-century Mishnah commentator</note> on the same passage of the MISHNAH. Let him who delights in these intellectual feasts unroll my own *philological commentary on sacred parenthesis, section II, at rule I, page 28 and following,* where I have discussed more on this argument.

## RULE IV.

There is a notable **ABUSE** of Sacred Scripture: If the **words** <note>original Greek: λέξεων</note> and **phrases** <note>original Greek: φράσεων</note> of the New Testament are illustrated from ingenious conjectures and fabricated synagogue ceremonies which, evidently, are destitute of historical credibility.

For if any narrator of the heavenly oracles takes for himself the license of invention, the sacred scripture is deprived of the **demonstrative power** <note>original Greek: ἀποδείξει</note> with which it prevails; and those who immoderately abuse their own genius in this way find, instead of treasure, coals—

**MATTHEW 6:2.** The word **TO SOUND A TRUMPET** <note>original Greek: σαλπίζειν (*salpizein*)</note> is derived from the trumpet-shaped vessels of the synagogue, called **shofrot** <note>original Hebrew: שׁוֹפָרוֹת (*shofrot*, the plural of shofar)</note>, by that most learned man, **STEPHANVS LE MOINE** <note>Stephanus Le Moine (1624–1689), a French Protestant theologian</note>. He claims these vessels had a narrow mouth but a wider, curved body, and were manufactured from brass or ringing metal so that if the Pharisees threw their alms in with great force, they would give back the ringing of a trumpet—as noted in his *Notes on Various Sacred Matters, page 73*. But from where, I ask, can it be proven that the vessels intended for alms were constructed in this manner? Nor is it likely that the **SAVIOR** would have called any kind of ringing sound a **trumpeting** <note>original Greek: σαλπισμόν (*salpismon*)</note>. Whatever the case may be, anyone can understand of their own accord that this observation shows more of a clever imagination than a likeness of probability. In a similar way:

**I TIMOTHY 3:15.** **FRANCISCVS BVRMANNVS** <note>Frans Burman (1628–1679), a Dutch theologian</note> thinks that **PAUL** was looking toward the pillars of the synagogue when he called the church the **PILLAR and GROUND of the truth** <note>original Greek: στύλον καὶ ἑδραίωμα (*stylon kai hedraiōma*)</note>, in his *Theological Disputations II: On Synagogues, Thesis XVI*. Some report, he says, that on Mount **SION** alone there were seven synagogues: which they believe were hinted at by those seven pillars with which it is read that Wisdom built her house, *Proverbs 9:1*. For in the middle of each synagogue there was a pillar, which the teacher would ascend to deliver words from its platform; thus the seven pillars stand for the seven synagogues. In this sense, the **CHURCH** could also be seen as being called by **PAUL** the **pillar and ground of the truth**, *1 Timothy 3:15*, that is, the **PILLAR**, or **CHAIR** <note>original Latin: *cathedra*</note>, from which sacred truth is preached and promulgated. What I think of this matter, I shall speak **without passion** <note>original Greek: ἄνευ πάθους (*aneu pathous*)</note>. And indeed, regarding the first of those interpreters (†) of this Pauline oracle who, having a greater insight into the truth, refer that predicate not to **THE CHURCH** <note>original Greek: τὴν ἐκκλησίαν (*tēn ekklēsian*)</note> but rather to the following words: I confess, profess, and maintain that their opinion is deservedly better and more sacred to me. For I am hardly led to believe that in this one short, continuous speech, the church is compared now with a *house*, and now with a *pillar of the house*. Nor would there be any connection with what precedes, where after the word "living" [God], the words "as after" <note>original Latin: *vt post*</note> are omitted through **ellipsis** <note>original Greek: κατ' ἔλλειψιν (*kat' elleipsin*)</note> from the common context, to be supplied from verse 14: *I am writing these things to you*. # PRELIMINARY DISSERTATION ON THE USE AND ABUSE OF ANCIENT SYNAGOGUES.

By a very ancient writer, it is expressly called the **ONLY HOUSE OF THE GODS** <note>original Greek: ΜΟΝΟΣ ΘΕΩΝ ΟΙΚΟΣ (*monos theōn oikos*)</note>. And **ARISTOPHANES** addresses **ARTEMIS** <note>The Greek goddess of the hunt, known as Diana to the Romans</note>, to whom **EPHESUS** was sacred, with these words in *The Clouds, lines 598 and following:*

->And you, the blessed one of EPHESUS,<-
->who possess the ALL-GOLDEN HOUSE.<-

Where the scholarly notes <note>original: *scholia*</note> say: *By "all-golden house," he means the most costly TEMPLE, which was one of the seven wonders.* This shrine, therefore, had **127 COLUMNS**, and thirty-six of them were intricately carved, just as **C. PLINY THE ELDER** <note>A famous Roman author and naturalist</note> recorded in his *Natural History, Book 36, Chapter 14.* Upon these **COLUMNS**, various legendary **INSCRIPTIONS** could be seen—**atheistic myths** <note>original Greek: μῦθοι ΑΘΕΟΙ (*mythoi atheoi*)</note> and vain **LIES** which the superstitious worshippers of the **UNKNOWN GOD** <note>original Greek: ΑΓΝΩΣΤΟΥ ΘΕΟΥ (*agnōstou theou*); a reference to Acts 17:23</note> boasted regarding the **EPIPHANIES** <note>original Greek: ΕΠΙΦΑΝΕΙΑΙΣ (*epiphaneiais*); divine appearances or manifestations</note> of their gods. **JEAN HARDOUIN** <note>A 17th-century French scholar and numismatist</note> displays a temple with four **COLUMNS** on a coin, in which stands **JUPITER**, designated by these letters: **Z. K. Y.**, that is, *Zeus Capitolinus the Most High*, or if you prefer, *The Supreme*. *See his Select Works, folio 638, Amsterdam edition.* Truly, this is cited by me only for the sake of illustration. The **GREAT MYSTERIES** (†) were very well known among the pagans, which were not open to everyone equally, but closed to most (*); toward which the secret and secluded **RITES OF CERES** <note>The goddess of agriculture, celebrated in the Eleusinian Mysteries</note> at Eleusis—a very famous village or town in Attica—especially point. There, everything performed by the initiates <note>original: *mystis*</note> in the sacred rites just mentioned was hidden in the deepest and most religious silence, and it was forbidden to speak of them. Nor is this surprising: for they were **MYSTERIES of IMPIETY** <note>original Greek: τῆς ΑΣΕΒΕΙΑΣ ΜΥΣΤΗΡΙΑ (*tēs asebeias mystēria*)</note>. Thus the profane pagan crowd, lacking the light of the holier Scripture, **even display their passions as MYSTERIES** <note>original Greek: καὶ τὰ πάθη αὐτῶν δεικνύουσι ΜΥΣΤΗΡΙΑ (*kai ta pathē autōn deiknyousi mystēria*)</note>; they even call their lusts and cravings "mysteries." This was recorded by **ATHENAGORAS**, a Christian philosopher whose memory is made famous a century after the birth of Christ, in his *Embassy for the Christians, Chapter 27.* Add to this **ISAAC CASAUBON** in his *16th Exercise against Baronius, number 42.* Nor do the **enigmatic EPHESIAN letters** <note>original Greek: ΕΦΕΣΙΑ γράμματα ΑΙΝΙΓΜΑΤΩΔΗ (*Ephesia grammata ainigmatōdē*); these were famous magical formulas or amulets associated with the city</note> escape anyone’s notice, being worthy of mention in this place. These things having been set forth from Greek antiquity—especially that of Ephesus—as they ought to be, the great **power** of the Pauline **antithesis** <note>The sharp contrast Paul draws between the pagan temple and the Christian Church</note> deserves to be explained: In the house, not of gods lacking life, but of the **LIVING GOD**, there are not many **pillars** <note>original Greek: στύλοι (*styloi*)</note> as in the pagan shrine at Ephesus, but...

ON THE INTERPRETATION OF THE NEW TESTAMENT.

### RULE V.

->THE USE OF HOLY SCRIPTURE IS NOT TO BE DISREGARDED<-

If the word <note>Greek: *lexis*</note> SYNAGOGUE <note>Greek: *synagōgē*</note>, or HOUSE OF PRAYER <note>Greek: *proseuchē*</note>, a type of synagogue, occurs in the New Testament with a manifest usage <note>Greek: *chrēsei*</note> referring to the JEWS, or to a certain Jewish ceremony, it is accepted as referring to the Jewish synagogue, and indeed to the ancient one, and is illustrated from that context.

IF the word mentioned in the GOSPELS is found clothed in these circumstances <note>Greek: *peristaseis*</note>, the matter is beyond all doubt. But in the ACTS, whenever it occurs in this manner, the same judgment must also be held. For the JEWS after the Dispersion <note>Greek: *tēn diasporan*</note> had their own SYNAGOGUE built by public authority in most cities of Greece, Syria, and Asia Minor. LUKE, the sacred historian, supplies examples in:

ACTS 9:2; 13:14; 14:1; 17:1, 10, 17; 18:4, 19; and others of the same kind. To be sure, there are those who cannot bring themselves to believe that the Gentiles once granted the Jews public worship in synagogues, as these rites were so different from their own institutions. But since they did not prohibit them from the *use of houses of prayer*, there remains for me no cause for doubt at all as to why the pagans <note>Latin: *ethnici*</note> would have denied synagogues to the Jewish nation. That fact clearly appears from the decree of the HALICARNASSIANS <note>People of Halicarnassus, an ancient Greek city</note> regarding this matter; although it is missing from the common editions of the books of JOSEPHUS <note>Flavius Josephus, the 1st-century Jewish historian</note>, the great man ISAAC VOSSIUS published it from a manuscript in his notes on *Catullus, page 313*. The celebrated GOTTFRIED OLEARIVS also reported this, illustrated with learned nighttime studies, in his *Observations on Matthew, page 170 and following*. It must furthermore be observed here that the HOUSE OF PRAYER <note>Greek: *proseuchē*</note> was a certain type of synagogue, since in the *synagogues, prayers* <note>Latin: *preces*</note> were poured out to GOD, as no one is unaware. From this, excellent light is shed upon the passage in:

ACTS 16:13. "Where a HOUSE OF PRAYER was thought to be" <note>Greek: *proseuchē einai*</note>, that is, where there was a *proseucha*: a fact which *is expressed in the following chapter, 17:1:* "where there was the SYNAGOGUE" <note>Greek: *hē synagōgē*</note>.

MATTHEW 6:5. where a clear allusion is made to the word <note>Greek: *lexei*</note> STANDING <note>Greek: *hestōtes*</note> in reference to the *standing* <note>Hebrew: *amud*, referring to the 'Amidah' or standing prayer</note> or the ceremony of praying, which was received by solemn use and custom both in the temple and in the synagogue; where it only incurred rebuke because they prayed with the goal THAT THEY MIGHT BE SEEN <note>Greek: *hopōs phanerōsi*</note> by men, that is, *that they might become visible to people*. (†)

### ->RULE VII.<-

*The new use of the Holy Scripture here is:*
*Words <note>Greek: lēxeis</note> and phrases of the New Testament that are somewhat obscure and emphatic <note>Greek: emphatikai</note> should be rendered clearer from the synagogue, provided other circumstances <note>Greek: peristasesi</note> allow it.*

For this is the primary goal of illustrating the New Testament through the ceremonies of the synagogue: that obscure oracles may be illuminated when the matter requires it. However, those things which already radiate with their own light are only obscured by an empty desire to "illuminate" them. It is often to be feared that such illumination—which consists of merely piling up the same words that mean the same thing without any added emphatic idea—introduces more darkness than light. See, for example, my observations on 

LUKE 2:46 under *Rule III*. Thus in 

LUKE 6:1. the phrase SECOND-FIRST SABBATH <note>Greek: *sabbaton deuteroprōton*; a famously difficult term likely referring to a specific day in the Jewish liturgical calendar</note> requires light. Therefore, praise is due to JOHN LIGHTFOOT, a man who, though he often violated this rule elsewhere, was highly skilled in Rabbinic literature, even if he sometimes rendered things doubtful...

## RULE VIII.

### THE FIRST ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE is contrary to the use demonstrated in Rule VII:

->*Beware of laboriously and pointlessly comparing very clear words <note>Greek: lexeis</note> or phrases <note>Greek: phraseis</note> of the New Covenant with terms used in the synagogue that involve no other specific or emphatic meaning beyond having the same sound.*<-

An illustration of this rule should be sought from the notes I added to Rule VII. Indeed, Stephanus Le Moine brought forward many such words <note>Greek: lexeis</note> in his *Notes on the Ancient Synagogue, page 22 and following*, some of which are of such a nature that you might rightly doubt whether they were even derived from the synagogue; very few actually reveal the core meaning of the sacred words. Among these, the names of the synagogue officials stand out above all others, for example: <term>Appointed officials</term> <note>Hebrew: memunim</note>, <term>Elders</term> <note>Hebrew: zeqenim</note>, <term>Providers</term> <note>Hebrew: parnassim</note>, and <term>Messengers of the congregation</term> <note>Hebrew: shluchei tzibur</note>. Some scholars compare these with the apostolic words <note>Greek: lexesin</note>: <term>Shepherds</term> <note>Greek: poimenes</note>, <term>Elders</term> <note>Greek: presbyteroi</note>, <term>Overseers</term> <note>Greek: episkopoi</note>, and <term>Angels of the church</term> <note>Greek: angeloi tēs ekklēsias</note> in *Revelation 1:20* (see Campegius Vitringa on this passage). I will not entirely condemn this practice, but I am an advisor and advocate that we learn to trade in these ideas more cautiously than others have. Hence, first, one must compare the *parallel passages of BOTH TESTAMENTS*, for example, *Jeremiah 3:15, Ezekiel 34:2, Malachi 2:7, 3:1*, where <term>Shepherds</term> and <term>Angels</term> are the names given to the ministers of the divine word. These are sent by God just like THE GREAT SHEPHERD <note>Greek: HO POIMĒN HO MEGAS</note> (*Isaiah 40:11, Ezekiel 34:23, John 14:11, Hebrews 13:20*), opening the way for mortals to blessed immortality; they have no less care for souls—which are dearer than gold or silver—than shepherds have for their sheep.

### RULE IX.

-> THE SECOND ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE, CONTRARY TO THE USE SHOWN IN RULE VII, IS THIS: <-

> Beware of attributing a synagogal **emphasis** <note>Greek: *emphaisin*</note> to the sacred words of the New Covenant—especially those concerning morality—and thereby stripping those same words of the **emphasis** they claim for themselves from the sacred context.

In other words, those emphases that are already very clear from the context do not need illustration sought from elsewhere, by the power of *Rule VII*. However, the mind must be carefully applied to avoid a situation where the innate meanings are deprived of their own strength by introduced emphases. This occurs in the usage of:

**JOHN 5:39**, regarding the emphatic word **SEARCH** <note>Greek: *EREUNATE*</note>. Jean Le Clerc, a very famous man who to this day still adorns and protects refined literature in Amsterdam, comments in the notes to the French New Testament edited by him at this passage: *You search the Scriptures, that is, you search for their hidden meanings.* <note>original French: "Vous cherchez les Ecritures, c'est à dire, vous en recherchez les sens cachez."</note> And a little later: *allegorical meanings.* <note>original French: "sens allegoriques."</note> The sum of his opinion comes to this: he thinks the Savior, the Best and Greatest, is rebuking the allegorical and kabbalistic interpretations of the **Scriptures** <note>Greek: *tōn GRAPHŌN*</note> that were approved in every way by the Jewish doctors of the synagogue at that time. In his *Ancient and Modern Library, volume 5, article 2, page 314*, he adds: *The very **force** <note>original French: "L'ENERGIE"; the power or internal meaning</note> of the Greek word seems to require it.* But in truth, since the word "You" <note>Greek: *hymeis*</note> is not placed before it, the word **SEARCH** <note>Greek: *EREUNATE*</note> should be understood in the imperative mood [as a command] rather than the indicative mood [as a statement of fact]. Thus, Jesus is urging a scrutiny of the divine scriptures that is accurate, diligent, and beneficial for the true students of his teaching. John Chrysostom, in his *40th Homily* on this passage, hit the mark regarding both the **emphasis** and the purpose of the verse exceptionally well: *For this reason,* he says, *to **dig through** <note>Greek: *DIASKAPTEIN*</note> them with...

...parallelism <note>original Greek: parallēlismon</note>: for indeed he was a Hebrew of Hebrews, that is, a Hebrew by nation and race, *Philippians 3:5*, and so was not at all inexperienced in Jewish rituals. Furthermore, Johannes Braun, in *Selected Sacred Works, book 1, chapter 3, page 52 and following*, learnedly contends that Christian proselytes from Judaism were found in the Corinthian church. It was especially a custom for these people that, because of the excellence of their flesh or kinship—through which they traced their genealogy from the pious patriarchs, especially ABRAHAM—they would, with a great but futile daring, claim for themselves unique rights and heavenly privileges, *Matthew 3:9; John 8:33, 39*. From this, they would grasp with both hands any occasion for glorying **in appearance, and not in heart** <note>original Greek: en prosōpō, kai ou kardia</note>, *verse 12*. From this, everyone naturally understands that the Apostle is here occupied in debunking this presumed opinion.

Since these things are so, I will briefly present the second rite of the synagogue which pertains to this. Formerly, "proselytes of justice" <note>original Hebrew: gere tzedek; these were full converts to Judaism who took on the whole Law</note> were initiated not only by circumcision and sacrifice, but also by **baptism** <note>original Hebrew: bi-tevilah; ritual immersion</note>, as Maimonides <note>A preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher and legal scholar</note> records in his *Arabic Preface to the Holy Things, page 274.* These same people were afterwards commanded to renounce their former births in heathendom, so that they would no longer recognize anyone among the gentiles **according to the flesh** <note>original Latin: secundum carnem</note>—that is, no father, mother, brother, or sister joined by close kinship—nor would they expect any rights from their former blood relationship. This occurred to them just as it once did to the citizens of Athens recovering from the plague, who "did not know themselves or their close associates," to use a Thucydidean phrase here along with JOHN SELDEN <note>A 17th-century English polymath and scholar of Jewish law</note> in *On the Natural and International Law according to the Teachings of the Hebrews, page 158, Strasbourg edition.*

Hence this canon was accepted in use among the Hebrew people: *Whoever was a blood relative to the proselyte while he was a gentile, is now no longer a blood relative.* Here, the term **FLESH** <note>original Hebrew: she’er basar</note> is used twice for a kinsman or blood relative, as it is in the Holy Language in *Genesis 37:27*. I would list the Talmudic passages which I have ready at hand, were it not that the matter admits no doubt and my pledge of brevity stands in the way. But I think this further point should not be overlooked: such a proselyte initiated into the synagogue rites—because his old kinship with heathendom was denied and a new citizenship in the synagogue was adopted—was formerly considered similar to a **newborn infant** <note>original Hebrew: katan she-nolad</note> and a **NEW CREATURE**, as seen in the *Gemara Yevamot <note>A section of the Talmud dealing with marriage and conversion laws</note>, folio 22, 1; 62, 1; and elsewhere.* You will find the reason for this title, and a quite ridiculous one at that, in *Bereshith Rabba <note>An ancient Jewish commentary on the book of Genesis</note>, section 39, collection 84.* Truly, PIERRE DU BOSC (†) judges this external ceremony learnedly: "It is true that **THE JEWS** pushed here the..."

### ON THE INTERPRETATION OF THE NEW TESTAMENT <note>original Latin: IN INTERPRETATIONE NOVI FOEDERIS</note>

...[taking] these things too far, and that they gave themselves over, as was their habit, to visions and chimeras. <note>original French: ici les choses trop loin, et qu'ils donnoient à leur ordinaire dans la vision et dans la chimere. Indeed, we no longer even prioritize the faithful **FATHERS**, from whom **CHRIST** came **ACCORDING TO THE FLESH** (*Romans 9:4–5*). They were even **TWICE AS MUCH** so as the missionaries who had converted them (*Matthew 23:15*). But concerning the Christian convert, the Apostle says: if anyone is **IN CHRIST**, through true **FAITH** working through love—since this **ALONE** has any power in Christ Jesus, and not **CIRCUMCISION** nor **UNCIRCUMCISION** (*Galatians 5:6*)—that person is finally a **NEW CREATION**. Indeed, this **FAITH** itself is the **NEW CREATION** (*Galatians 6:15 compared with 5:6*). For to a person who truly believes, all old things have truly passed away; behold! **ALL THINGS ARE MADE NEW**. The "new creation" of a synagogue convert was merely a civil and human institution—

### PRELIMINARY DISSERTATION ON THE USE AND ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE

In John 6:44, Jesus Christ affirms that no one can come to Him by true faith "unless the Father draws him" <note>original Greek: *ἐὰν μὴ ὁ πατὴρ ΕΛΚΥΣΗ αὐτὸν* (ean mē ho patēr helkysē auton)</note>, or unless the heavenly Father has pulled him. For this reason, they were called "drawn proselytes" <note>original Hebrew: גרוים גירורים (gerim gerurim)</note> in the *Gemara* <note>the part of the Talmud containing rabbinical commentary</note> in the chapters *Avoda Zara* 24.1 and *Yevamot* 79.1. To be sure, no mention is made of the Jewish synagogue in the context of the verse itself; for this reason, I would hardly think that the Supreme Orator <note>referring to Jesus</note> had this in mind (as discussed in Section 1, Rule 2). Yet, if anyone should wish to employ a comparison here, they should not neglect: 1. the emphatic contrast; 2. above all, the verbal and thematic parallelism in the Bible (*Song of Solomon 1:4, Jeremiah 31:3, John 6:65, 12:32*); and finally, 3. seeking a much fuller and more solid illustration from a more sacred theology.

In a similar way, there are those who think that the "birth" <note>original Greek: ΓΕΝΝΗΣΙΝ (gennēsin)</note> which happens "from above" <note>original Greek: ΑΝΩΘΕΝ (anōthen)</note> mentioned in John 3:5 and 1 Peter 1:23 receives light from these same synagogue ceremonies. I will not pick a quarrel with them, provided that a comparative contrast <note>original Greek: *ἀντιθετικὴ* (antithetikē)</note> is established as the rule recommends, and that the following observations are noted, which were sketched with an elegant brush by Henry Dodwell <note>1641–1711, a prominent Anglo-Irish scholar and Camden Professor of History at Oxford</note>, the most celebrated historian and Camden reader at Oxford Academy, in his *Second Dissertation on Irenaeus*, page 113:

> If the Rabbis recognize any new birth of the Spirit in their Baptism, or any Divine Presence <note>original Hebrew: *Schechinam* (Shekhinah), referring to the dwelling or settling of the divine presence of God</note> common to all their people—whether from Baptism or even from Circumcision—they did not receive these traditions from their ancestors of the apostolic times. Rather, like many other things, they transcribed them into their own more recent hypotheses from the accepted dogmas of the Christians. Seeing these things claimed by our people, they decided to claim them for their own glory, lest they appear inferior to us.

But more will be given on this matter in:

...and political matters, not only is a parallelism and comparison established, but their very origin is clearly derived from these: to which the sacrament of the BAPTISM OF JOHN, the *Forerunner* <note>original Greek: τοῦ Προδρόμου (tou Prodromou)</note>, Matthew 3:2, 8, 11, especially belongs. Some believe they have sufficiently weighty reasons to trace its birth from the proselytism of the Old Covenant <note>original: S.V., likely referring to the "Ancient Synagogue" or "Old Covenant"</note>.

Renowned men have contended with one another on this matter, putting forward arguments on both sides such that you might rightly remain hesitant and doubtful as to which opinion you should subscribe to. However, I will not make these controversies my own, nor am I armed with such incredible boldness as to take it upon myself to settle such great disputes. Meanwhile, since the thread of my own argument—the web of which I have begun to weave for this purpose—leads me to a point where I am forced to declare my opinion on this matter, if I do so with the candid effort of a mind devoted to truth, no one will interpret it unfavorably. Therefore, as far as the COMPARISON or *parallelism* is concerned, which the *analogy of faith* <note>original Greek: ἀναλογία πίστεως (analoga pisteos) — the principle that scripture should be interpreted in a way consistent with the rest of Christian doctrine</note> favors, I admit it with both hands (as Rule 1 has already taught), and I contend that this USE of the Old Covenant is most elegant. Thus, for example, CAMPEGIUS VITRINGA <note>1659–1722, a prominent Dutch theologian and Hebraist</note> in his *Sacred Observations, Book II, Chapter VI, page 321*, not inconveniently (in my judgment) compared Christian infant baptism with the baptism of a <term>minor proselyte <note>original Hebrew: גר קטן (ger katan) — a child from a non-Jewish background who is converted to Judaism</note></term>, a noteworthy passage concerning which occurs in the *GEMARA KETUBOT, folio 11, column 1* <note>The Gemara is the part of the Talmud containing rabbinical commentary; Ketubot is the volume dealing with marriage contracts</note>. But if the very ORIGIN of John's baptism is derived from the Old Covenant, I judge that this must be noted as an ABUSE. For both *historical* and, especially, *theological* precision stand against such an attempt.

I. *Historical* precision <note>original Greek: ἀκρίβεια (akribeia)</note> stands in the way. For it cannot yet be admitted as so certainly explored and beyond all doubt—the primary point and the very issue at stake: *Was the baptism of proselytes already in use in the age of JOHN THE BAPTIST <note>original Greek: τοῦ ΒΑΠΤΙΣΤΟΥ (tou Baptistou)</note>, or not?* Certainly, the Talmudic writers, in investigating the origins of their own ceremonies, have long since exhausted their credibility among all skilled evaluators of these matters. Nor can this historical question of the greatest importance be solidly decided from the sacred records of the New Covenant. For NICODEMUS, *John 3:9, 10*, is rebuked by the SAVIOR not because of an ignorance of *proselyte baptism*, but because of the unknown nature of the *baptism* of THE BAPTIST; which, however, should have been sufficiently clear and explored by him, as a GREAT TEACHER of Israel <note>original Greek: DOCTORI τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ (Doktori tou Israel)</note>, following the report made by the public delegates sent by the order of the higher council, the SANHEDRIN <note>the supreme legal and religious assembly of the Jews</note>, *Matthew 3:7, John 1:19–21*. Finally, it is true that FLAVIUS JOSEPHUS <note>a first-century Romano-Jewish historian</note> speaks of the baptism of JOHN as a known thing...

*Book 18, chapter 7, page 626; namely, that he commanded the Jews who were devoted to piety and justice* **to come together for baptism** <note>original Greek: ΒΑΠΤΙΣΜΩ συνιέναι (baptismo synienai)</note>; *for in this way, the* **baptism** <note>original Greek: ΒΑΠΤΗΣΙΝ (baptisin)</note> *would appear acceptable to Him (God), as they were not using it as a plea for certain sins, but for the* **purification of the BODY** <note>original Greek: ἁγνείᾳ τοῦ ΣΩΜΑΤΟΣ (hagneia tou somatos)</note>, *since the* **SOUL** <note>original Greek: ΨΥΧΗΣ (psyches)</note> *had already been* **PREVIOUSLY PURIFIED** <note>original Greek: ΠΡΟΕΚΚΕΚΑΘΑΡΜΕΝΗΣ (proekkekatharmenes)</note> *by righteousness, and so forth.* But what, I ask, follows from this? However, one cannot yet rightly conclude from this that the celebrated baptism was more recent than the one which held sway in the Jewish synagogue. If you were even to say that in that first century the **Immersion of the Proselyte** <note>original Hebrew: טבילת גר (Tevilat Ger) — the ritual bath used for converts to Judaism</note> already had a place, you would be saying nothing far from the truth, and you would also cease to wonder why FLAVIVS <note>Flavius Josephus (c. 37–100 AD), the famous Jewish-Roman historian</note> spoke of John's **baptism** <note>original Greek: βαπτισμῷ (baptismo)</note> as a well-known thing. Were not the **various baptisms** <note>original Greek: διαφόροι βαπτισμοὶ (diaphoroi baptismoi)</note>—mentioned in *Hebrews 9:10*—which looked solely toward the **purity of the BODY** <note>original Greek: ἁγνείαν τοῦ ΣΩΜΑΤΟΣ (hagneian tou somatos)</note>, very well known among those Jews who were little concerned with the purity of the mind? Indeed, even the Gentiles could more easily give credence to this report by Flavius, because it is certain that various symbols of internal **purification** <note>original Greek: καθάρσεως (katharseos)</note>, such as washings, lustral rites, and various types of expiations, were accepted in use among them. Regarding such **baptisms** <note>original Greek: βαπτισμοῖς (baptismois)</note>, SOCRATES spoke eloquently: (*) **"All these things,"** he says, **"are able to make a person PURE both in terms of the BODY and in terms of the SOUL."** Certainly, I judge it especially worthy of observation here that in composing his history, JOSEPHUS was not so free from bias that he did not also adapt his style in every part to the understanding and spirit of the Greeks and Romans. For in order to favor them, he either omitted in bad faith (†) those institutions which he foresaw would be a disgrace to the Jewish nation or would be mocked by them, or else he reported them differently than was proper, incautiously reconciling them with the ceremonies of superstitious paganism. (††) I point these things out with the intention that it may clearly appear from JOSEPHUS's account—even if we were willing to grant to any liberal hand—that he wrote about the baptism of JOHN in such a way...

[...that he] wrote so that the **immersion of proselytes** <note>original Hebrew: טבילת גר (Tevilat Ger) — the ritual bath for converts to Judaism</note> seems to have been a thing already well enough known and practiced beforehand, and appears to have differed from John's only in its purpose and true nature. However, it can by no means be established that the Jewish **immersion of the proselyte** <note>original Hebrew: טבילת הגר (Tevilat Ha-Ger)</note> is older than the baptism of the **Precursor** <note>original Greek: τοῦ Προδρόμου (tou Prodromou) — a traditional title for John the Baptist as the one who ran ahead of Christ</note>. For by the same logic, one would have to conclude that the origins of the Johannine sacrament should be sought not only in the baptism of the synagogue—through which the Jewish people intended the cleansing of the body rather than the mind—but even in the washings of the Gentiles <note>non-Jewish nations</note> which had already been in use for a long time. Indeed, the **phrasing** <note>original Greek: Φράσις (Phrasis)</note> used by **Flavius** <note>Flavius Josephus</note> is very similar to the wording used by Socrates; this point gains even more strength if one considers our attached **judgment** <note>original Greek: ἐπίκρισιν (epikrisin)</note> regarding Josephus's history. 

And the profane opinion of **Marsham** <note>Sir John Marsham (1602–1685), an English historian who argued that Jewish rites often imitated Egyptian ones</note> certainly points in this direction, where he openly derives the ultimate origin of baptism from the Egyptians in his *Chronological Canon*, pages 193 and 253. But indeed, the former argument [concerning the synagogue], as I have shown so far, is devoid of arguments that have the power to prove it; the latter [the Egyptian origin] is asserted with greater ease than it can be proven, especially since a very great difference exists between John's baptism and Egyptian washings. 

It remains, therefore, that we should attribute the origin of the synagogue’s baptism—in which a greater, and entirely external and material, similarity with John's **baptism** <note>original Greek: βαπτισμῷ (baptismo)</note> is detected—to a certain Jewish **perverse imitation** <note>original Greek: κακοζηλίᾳ (kakozēlia) — a term for a distorted or misguided copying of a style</note>. Thus, it becomes likely that the Jews, already in the age of Christ, began gradually to adopt John's baptism, and in the following apostolic centuries, they continued with even greater zeal to imitate the Christians who were baptizing. In this way, they were "mixing squares with circles" <note>a Latin idiom for trying to reconcile two incompatible things</note>, retaining **circumcision** from Judaism while introducing **baptism** from Christian practice. See Rule I on 2 Corinthians 5:16, and reread here the words of **H. Dodwell** <note>Henry Dodwell (1641–1711), a scholar known for his works on early Church history</note> recorded under that same rule. And for this reason, historical **precision** <note>original Greek: ἀκρίβεια (akribeia)</note> stands in the way of deriving the origin of Christian baptism from the Jewish synagogue.

Furthermore, a second obstacle is theological **precision** <note>original Greek: ἀκρίβεια (akribeia)</note>. For the **Savior** <note>Latin: SERVATOR — i.e., Jesus Christ</note> Himself suggests in Matthew 21:25 that the baptism of John was not **from men** <note>original Greek: ἐξ ἀνθρώπων (ex anthrōpōn)</note>, and thus not **from the SYNAGOGUE** <note>original Greek: ἐκ ΣΥΝΑΓΩΓΗΣ (ek SYNAGŌGĒS)</note>, but rather **FROM HEAVEN** <note>original Greek: ΕΞ ΟΥΡΑΝΟΥ (EX OURANOU)</note>; that is, by way of contrast, it received its origin from God. The Pharisees certainly did not want to admit this openly, yet they did not dare to deny it. 

Therefore, baptism is rightly and deservedly numbered among the **MYSTERIES OF GOD** <note>original Greek: ΜΥΣΤΗΡΙΑ ΘΕΟΥ (MYSTĒRIA THEOU)</note> mentioned in 1 Corinthians 4:1, of which the apostles were once the **stewards** <note>original Greek: οἰκονόμοι (oikonomoi)</note>, and the ministers of the divine word are today. For it is a **mystery** of the revealed Christian religion and a means of salvation, just like the other more sacred mysteries—previously unknown and divinely instituted in the **New Covenant** <note>Latin: N. F. (Novum Foedus)</note> in place of the **circumcision** of the **Old Covenant** <note>Latin: V. F. (Vetus Foedus)</note>, as seen in Colossians 2:11. 

But, you say, no one has ever called this into doubt; rather, the dispute is still before the judge as to whether the supreme Master of the Christian religion might have approved a **rite of baptism** received from the synagogue and established it as the **washing of regeneration**. This is understood most clearly from the fact that mortals, in their reckless audacity, did not hesitate to attribute to this human, political ceremony—devoid of all internal power—those most **emphatic** <note>original Greek: ἐμφατικώτατα (emphatikōtata)</note> names, such as **"new birth"** or **"regeneration,"** and likewise **"new creature."** These were the terms by which both the **SAVIOR** and His apostles rightly and most deservedly expressed the reality and internal efficacy of baptism. ### RULE III.

->*The USE of the Ancient Synagogue is new:*<-

If some ceremonies of the APOSTOLIC CHURCHES are compared with the clear, and by no means obscure, rites of the Ancient Synagogue—especially those that savor of the purity of the ancient Jewish church of the Old Covenant—in such a way that nothing forced, nothing invented by human ingenuity, and nothing far-fetched is applied: then, above all, the obvious difference between the two must be investigated with the most refined diligence.

I see that this rule is formulated in such a way that it is my duty to shed some light upon it. Before all else, no more doubt remains in my mind that some similarity is found between the ceremonies of the synagogue and some of those of the apostolic churches, particularly among those that approach more closely the genuine form of the ancient Jewish church. Therefore, I am persuaded that these were introduced into the church by the apostles, not so much from a vain desire to imitate the synagogue, but rather because they were drawn from its simplicity, joined with the highest gravity and holiness. Hence, while the comparison with the synagogue—which serves for illustration—is not to be blamed, the difference in the varying <term>circumstances</term> <note>original Greek: περιστάσεων (peristaseon) — referring to the specific historical or ritual contexts surrounding an event</note> on both sides must be shown so that no room is left for fiction. The parallelism of the church ceremonies, especially those of the Old Testament (since the apostles, as most solemn men, had these primarily in view), must be called into counsel with all diligence and zeal. Furthermore, if an <term>analogy</term> <note>original Greek: ἀναλογία (analogia)</note> of even some *civil* synagogue ceremony is detected in the apostolic discipline of the church, it must be acknowledged here as being rather of divine law. So that my meaning may strike the eyes more clearly, I myself will establish a comparison of some CEREMONIES found in the APOSTOLIC CHURCHES with those of the SYNAGOGUE, and indeed, by the method I have stated.

The Apostles employed a similar <term>reading</term> <note>original Greek: ἀνάγνωσιν (anagnosin)</note>.

### PRELIMINARY DISSERTATION ON THE USE AND ABUSE OF THE ANCIENT SYNAGOGUE.
<meta>catchword: More</meta>

*2 Corinthians 1:1, 13; 1 Timothy 4:13.* They were mindful of the same institution as the learned man and expert in the Mosaic law, Ezra (*Nehemiah 8:3*), who for that reason is called a **scribe skilled in the law of Moses** <note>original Hebrew: *sopher mahir be-torat Mosheh*</note> (*Ezra 7:6*), and to whose era some attribute the origin of the Jewish synagogues. *See also Acts 15:21.* Indeed, this reading of both the books of Moses and the prophets was kept entirely separate from all superstitious abuse as well as from the various synagogal interpretations.

II. **Prayers and fasts were joined together in the synagogue.** This same discipline was observed in the apostolic church, led by the genuine students of the ancient Jewish tradition, *2 Samuel 12:16; Ezra 8:23; Nehemiah 1:4; 2 Chronicles 20:3.* Yet, all abuse was removed from it.

III. **"AMEN" was shouted aloud in the synagogue.** The apostolic churches used this very ritual (*1 Corinthians 14:16*), intending to imitate the purity of the customs of the ancient Hebrew nation, *Deuteronomy 27:16 and following; Nehemiah 5:13; 1 Chronicles 16:36.* In former times, the Jews hardly ever used that word "AMEN" outside of the synagogue: (*) but Christians used it even in their private prayers, at the instruction of their Teacher himself, *Matthew 6:13.* (†)

IV. **Collectors of alms, called <term>charity collectors</term> <note>original Hebrew: *gabba’ei tzedakah*</note>, were once found in the synagogue.** In the same way, the nature of the church in Jerusalem required that seven managers, or <term>deacons</term> <note>from the Greek *diakonos*, meaning a servant or helper</note>, be chosen to care for the poor, *Acts 6:2 and following.* However, that office [in the synagogue] was a permanent one, whereas this [in the church] was less so.

V. **Excommunication from the synagogue**, *John 9:22; 12:42; 16:2,* together with flogging—viewed as a civil and human punishment, *Matthew 10:17; 23:34; Acts 5:40*—and other dreadful curses, *was a solemn practice among the Jews.* Similarly, excommunication was adopted in the apostolic churches, *Acts 8:20; 1 Corinthians 5:4, 5, 13; 1 Timothy 1:20,* but the punishment that followed this was miraculous and belonged to divine law. *Compare Ezra 10:8.*

(*) It is expressly written in the *Jerusalem Talmud, Berachot, folio 13, 3*: **"They did not answer 'Amen' in the Temple."** <note>original Hebrew: *tenu lo hayu onin amen be-veit ha-miqdash*</note> What did they say instead? **"Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."** <note>original Hebrew abbreviation: *B[arukh] Sh[em] K[evod] m[alkhuto] l[e-olam] v[a-ed]*</note> See also the *Babylonian Talmud, Joshua, folio 66, 1* and the commentary <note>original Greek: *scholion*</note> on the *Babylonian Talmud, Taanith, folio 16, 2.*

## RULE IV.

### This Rule concerns the ABUSE of the Ancient Synagogue:

> When the JEWISH SYNAGOGUE is thought to provide a sort of blueprint, according to which a certain and permanent form of the entire GOVERNMENT OF THE APOSTOLIC CHURCHES was modeled by the Apostles.

The most strenuous defenders of a certain hierarchy of ecclesiastical rule today dispute with great passion whether the form of the apostolic church was monarchical <note>Rule by one person, like a bishop or pope.</note> or aristocratic <note>Rule by a group of elders or leaders.</note>. These same men try to persuade themselves and others that they have discovered a most elegant blueprint in the Jewish synagogue—not just in the temple and the Jerusalem Sanhedrin <note>The supreme legal and religious council of the Jews.</note>—according to which the Christian church was organized. To prove what they desire, they appeal primarily to similar names of persons whose work involved the government of the synagogue and the administration of the primitive church. 

But those who believe the entire form of the church should be sought from the synagogue in this way cannot be cleared of the ABUSE of the ancient synagogue, and they achieve nothing despite their great effort. For just as most of the offices designated by these names are doubtful, uncertain, and shrouded in the dark night of obscurity, so too some names used in the apostolic churches were either completely unknown in the synagogue, or, though they seem similar to synagogal terms at first glance, they are foreign to synagogal usage and denote something far different—as will become clear from what follows. 

Indeed, there are synagogal institutions and names mentioned in the synagogue of which no mention at all is made in the apostolic church; this can be learned from the example of the <term>ten idle men</term> <note>Latin: *decem otioforum*; Hebrew: *batlanim*. These were ten men of leisure who were paid or volunteered to be available for every service to ensure a quorum (minyan) was present.</note>. Nor did it ever occur to the apostles to introduce into the Christian church a kind of worldly and civil empire, the most distinct traces of which are found in the government of the Jewish synagogue. Hence, the principal and chief office of those known as the <term>rulers of the synagogue</term> <note>Greek: *archisynagogōn*</note>...

<summary>The author warns against the scholarly mistake of assuming the early Christian Church was an exact structural replica of the Jewish Synagogue, arguing that many titles and roles functioned differently in each context.</summary>
